literature.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 中国国家监测数据(2010-2023年)显示总体病例死亡率约为4.8%。医院针对重症或危重症患者的队列研究报告显示出显著更高的死亡率,范围从12%到30%。 [10.3389/fcimb.2026.2002250]
入院IL-6水平随着疾病严重程度增加而升高,在重度病例中达到61.4 pg/mL(p < 0.001)。重症患者初始CD4 + T细胞计数较低(167 vs. 420 cells/μL;p = 0.036),并且一周后的CD4/CD8比值也较低(0.5 vs. [10.1038/s41598-026-79348-7]
在内部验证组队列研究中,ROC曲线下面积为0.841(95% CI:0.736–0.930)。根据训练组队列研究中的最大Youden指数,确定最佳截断概率为0.2053。当该截断概率应用于验证组队列研究时,模型表现出0.944(95% CI:0.742–0.990)的敏感性和0.698(95% CI:0.565–0.805)的特异性。 [10.1186/s12879-026-14844-9]
综述得出结论,人类发热伴血小板减少综合征病例通过不同的监测系统进行报告,而小型哺乳动物和外寄生虫的感染情况则主要记录在另一套独立的文献中。这种缺乏整合导致了在该地区估算发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒真实负担的困难。综述还强调了结合人类和动物数据对于全面理解疾病的重要性。 [10.17605/osf.io/uqrjb]

key_findings_en: National surveillance data from China (2010-2023) report an overall case fatality rate of approximately 4.8%. Hospital-based cohorts of severe or critically ill patients report substantially higher rates, ranging from 12% to 30%. [10.3389/fcimb.2026.2002250]

Admission IL-6 levels increased with disease severity, reaching 61.4 pg/mL in severe cases (p < 0.001). Critical illness patients had lower initial CD4 + T-cell counts (167 vs. 420 cells/μL; p = 0.036) and a lower one-week CD4/CD8 ratio (0.5 vs. [10.1038/s41598-026-79348-7]

In the internal validation cohort, the area under the ROC curve was 0.841 (95% CI: 0.736–0.930). Based on the maximum Youden index in the training cohort, the optimal cutoff probability was established at 0.2053. [10.1186/s12879-026-14844-9]

The mean annual incidence rate was 3.27 per 100,000 population, with annual rates ranging from 1.50 to 4.74 per 100,000. The highest estimated mean annual incidence rates were observed in Mashan Town (15.92 per 100,000), Shuangquan Town (12.57 per 100,000), and Xiaoli Town (8.68 per 100,000). [10.3389/fepid.2026.1829686]

The review concludes that human cases of SFTS are reported through separate surveillance systems, while infection in small mammals and ectoparasites is documented in a largely separate literature. This lack of integration leads to challenges in estimating the true burden of SFTS virus in the region. [10.17605/osf.io/uqrjb]

news.headline_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 一项科学综述发表在《Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology》上,将发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒的免疫逃逸机制与临床治疗挑战联系起来。该综述强调了该病毒破坏宿主免疫通路的能力,导致严重的疾病结果。 [news-9b638d8c1046c845]
一项全面调查发现,大别山布尼亚病毒在传播和临床结果方面存在地理差异,内陆省份感染病例数量高但死亡率较低,而沿海省份感染病例较少但致死率较高。 [news-d1e2e5b30efdf3bf]
一项范围综述确定了广泛参与严重发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)维持和传播的动物宿主,包括家畜、家周哺乳动物、自由活动的野生动物以及家庭宠物。综述还记录了中国威海一家貂养殖场发生的一起暴发,其中两例人类病例与该病毒有关。 [news-d3fc40681e3a0acb]
开发了一种机器学习模型,用于预测发热伴血小板减少综合征患者住院期间的死亡率,基于病毒、免疫和炎症生物标志物。该模型进行了内部验证,并显示出0.841的受试者工作特征曲线下面积。 [news-c82573173292a8d6]
发热伴血小板减少综合征是一种由蜱传播的传染病,主要通过感染蜱的叮咬传播。如果病情严重,该疾病可能致命,日本患者的病死率约为10–30%。犬猫也可感染发热伴血小板减少综合征,并且有从感染动物直接传播给人类的情况。 [news-28cae79b2cf99165]

papers.title: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus: immune evasion, therapeutic landscape, and vaccine prospects
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne bunyavirus that poses a growing public health threat. National surveillance data from China (2010-2023) report an overall case fatality rate of approximately 4.8%. However, hospital-based cohorts of severe or critically ill patients report substantially higher rates, ranging from 12% to 30%. Despite its designation as a WHO priority pathogen in 2017, no vaccine has been approved, although a first-in-human Phase I/II trial of an mRNA vaccine candidate was initiated in 2025, and favipiravir, the only authorized antiviral (Japan, 2024), remains of debated clinical benefit, leaving a widening gap between mechanistic understanding and clinical translation. This gap is rooted in the virus’s ability to dismantle the very immune pathways on which vaccines and antivirals depend. The non-structural protein NSs sequesters TBK1, IRF3, and STAT1/STAT2 into viroplasm-like structures, while the nucleoprotein NP induces autophagy-mediated degradation of cGAS and MAVS, collectively diminishing type I interferon responses, impairing B-cell and T-cell immunity, and permitting the dysregulated cytokine storm that is associated with multi-organ failure. These same mechanisms explain why vaccine candidates that perform well in immunocompromised (IFNAR−/− or STAT2−/−) mouse models have not translated to immunocompetent or aged populations, and why antiviral efficacy collapses at high viral loads or late treatment initiation. Unlike prior reviews that treat pathogenesis, antivirals, and vaccines as separate topics, this review integrates them into a single framework linking viral immune evasion to the failure modes of current countermeasures, and identifies the specific obstacles that must be overcome before clinical translation: missing correlates of protection, immunocompromised animal models, and reassortment-driven antigenic diversity. We conclude by outlining priority directions, including AI-assisted antigen design, host-directed and combination therapies, standardized animal models, and integrated One Health surveillance.

analysis.summary_en: This review addresses the growing public health threat posed by Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), an emerging tick-borne bunyavirus. It examines the challenges in developing effective vaccines and antivirals, emphasizing the virus's immune evasion mechanisms that hinder clinical translation. The study integrates findings on SFTSV's pathogenesis, therapeutic landscape, and vaccine prospects, highlighting the need for improved correlates of protection, more relevant animal models, and strategies to address antigenic diversity. The review underscores the limitations of current approaches, particularly the failure of vaccine candidates in immunocompetent populations and the debated clinical benefit of favipiravir. The findings suggest that understanding the virus's ability to disrupt immune pathways is critical for advancing therapeutic and preventive strategies. The evidence is based on national surveillance data, mechanistic studies, and clinical trial reports, with a moderate confidence level due to the reliance on existing literature and the absence of new experimental data.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱媒 Bunyavirus,对公共卫生构成日益增长的威胁。本研究旨在解决针对SFTSV的干预措施在机制理解与临床转化之间的差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究是对现有文献和数据的综述,重点聚焦于SFTSV及其临床意义。研究利用了中国国家监测数据(2010-2023年),并讨论了当前疫苗和抗病毒药物方法的局限性。
elements_zh.methods: 研究方法包括对已发表数据的全面分析,涵盖监测报告、临床试验和机制研究。综述将关于免疫逃逸、治疗前景及疫苗的发现整合到一个统一框架中。
elements_zh.main_results: 中国国家监测数据(2010-2023年)显示总体病例死亡率约为4.8%。医院针对重症或危重症患者的队列研究报告显示出显著更高的死亡率,范围从12%到30%。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 非结构蛋白NSs将TBK1、IRF3以及STAT1/STAT2隔离到类似病毒质粒的结构中,而核蛋白NP则通过自噬介导cGAS和MAVS的降解,共同抑制I型干扰素反应,损害B细胞和T细胞免疫,并允许与多器官衰竭相关的失调性细胞因子风暴的发生。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些机制也解释了为何在免疫缺陷(IFNAR−/−或STAT2−/−)小鼠模型中表现良好的疫苗候选药物未能在免疫正常或老年人群中实现转化,以及为何抗病毒药物在高病毒载量或晚期治疗启动时疗效会下降。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究强调了机制理解与临床转化之间的差距,指出需要改进保护相关指标、开发更相关的动物模型,并制定应对由重组驱动的抗原多样性的策略。

papers.title_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒:免疫逃逸、治疗前景及疫苗展望
papers.source_body_en: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is an emerging tick-borne bunyavirus that poses a growing public health threat. National surveillance data from China (2010-2023) report an overall case fatality rate of approximately 4.8%. However, hospital-based cohorts of severe or critically ill patients report substantially higher rates, ranging from 12% to 30%. Despite its designation as a WHO priority pathogen in 2017, no vaccine has been approved, although a first-in-human Phase I/II trial of an mRNA vaccine candidate was initiated in 2025, and favipiravir, the only authorized antiviral (Japan, 2024), remains of debated clinical benefit, leaving a widening gap between mechanistic understanding and clinical translation. This gap is rooted in the virus’s ability to dismantle the very immune pathways on which vaccines and antivirals depend. The non-structural protein NSs sequesters TBK1, IRF3, and STAT1/STAT2 into viroplasm-like structures, while the nucleoprotein NP induces autophagy-mediated degradation of cGAS and MAVS, collectively diminishing type I interferon responses, impairing B-cell and T-cell immunity, and permitting the dysregulated cytokine storm that is associated with multi-organ failure. These same mechanisms explain why vaccine candidates that perform well in immunocompromised (IFNAR−/− or STAT2−/−) mouse models have not translated to immunocompetent or aged populations, and why antiviral efficacy collapses at high viral loads or late treatment initiation. Unlike prior reviews that treat pathogenesis, antivirals, and vaccines as separate topics, this review integrates them into a single framework linking viral immune evasion to the failure modes of current countermeasures, and identifies the specific obstacles that must be overcome before clinical translation: missing correlates of protection, immunocompromised animal models, and reassortment-driven antigenic diversity. We conclude by outlining priority directions, including AI-assisted antigen design, host-directed and combination therapies, standardized animal models, and integrated One Health surveillance.
papers.abstract_zh: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱媒 Bunyavirus,对公共卫生构成日益增长的威胁。中国国家监测数据显示(2010-2023年),总体病例死亡率约为4.8%。然而,医院针对重症或危重症患者的队列研究报告显示出显著更高的死亡率,范围从12%到30%。尽管该病毒在2017年被世界卫生组织列为优先病原体,但目前尚无疫苗获批,尽管一项针对mRNA 疫苗候选药物的人体首次临床I/II期试验已于2025年启动,且favipiravir作为唯一获批的抗病毒药物(日本,2024年)仍存在临床疗效争议,导致机制理解与临床转化之间的差距不断扩大。这一差距源于病毒能够破坏其治疗手段(疫苗和抗病毒药物)所依赖的免疫通路。非结构蛋白NSs将TBK1、IRF3以及STAT1/STAT2隔离到类似病毒质粒的结构中,而核蛋白NP则通过自噬介导cGAS和MAVS的降解,共同抑制I型干扰素反应,损害B细胞和T细胞免疫,并允许与多器官衰竭相关的失调性细胞因子风暴的发生。这些机制也解释了为何在免疫缺陷(IFNAR−/−或STAT2−/−)小鼠模型中表现良好的疫苗候选药物未能在免疫正常或老年人群中实现转化,以及为何抗病毒药物在高病毒载量或晚期治疗启动时疗效会下降。与以往将发病机制、抗病毒药物和疫苗视为独立主题的综述不同,本文将它们整合到一个统一框架中,将病毒免疫逃逸与当前干预措施的失败模式联系起来,并指出了在临床转化前必须克服的具体障碍:保护相关指标的缺失、免疫缺陷动物模型的局限性以及由重组驱动的抗原多样性。我们最后概述了优先方向,包括AI辅助的抗原设计、针对宿主的治疗及联合疗法、标准化动物模型以及整合的One Health 监测。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)是一种新兴的蜱媒 Bunyavirus,对公共卫生构成日益增长的威胁。本研究旨在解决针对SFTSV的干预措施在机制理解与临床转化之间的差距。

papers.title: Explainable machine learning integrating virological and immune-inflammatory biomarkers for in-hospital mortality prediction in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome
papers.abstract: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), characterized by an excessive inflammatory response and impaired adaptive immunity, is associated with a high risk of mortality. This study aims to establish and validate a machine learning (ML)-based predictive model integrating clinical and immune-inflammatory biomarkers for in-hospital mortality in patients with SFTS. A total of 238 patients, including 177 survivors and 61 non-survivors, were divided by stratified random sampling into a training cohort ( n = 167) and an internal validation cohort ( n = 71) at a 7:3 ratio. Features were selected from the intersection of Boruta, Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator (LASSO), and random forest recursive feature elimination (RF-RFE). Model hyperparameters were optimized exclusively within the training cohort using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation, with the internal validation cohort reserved for final evaluation. Model performance was then assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration plots, and decision curve analysis (DCA). SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) was employed to improve model interpretability. To facilitate individualized risk estimation, the selected model was presented as a nomogram and incorporated into an interactive web-based calculator. The final logistic regression model incorporated four predictors: SFTSV RNA load, CD3+CD4+ T-cell count, IL-6, and PCT. In the internal validation cohort, the area under the ROC curve was 0.841 (95% CI: 0.736–0.930). Based on the maximum Youden index in the training cohort, the optimal cutoff probability was established at 0.2053. When this cutoff was applied to the validation cohort, the model yielded a sensitivity of 0.944 (95% CI: 0.742–0.990) and specificity of 0.698 (95% CI: 0.565–0.805). The model also demonstrated a Brier score of 0.139 (95% CI: 0.094–0.189) and potential net clinical benefit. We present an interpretable predictive model based on viral, immune, and inflammatory biomarkers for predicting in-hospital mortality in patients with SFTS. A multicenter prospective evaluation is highly recommended prior to its clinical use.

papers.full_text: Abstract Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS), caused by Dabie bandavirus, carries a case fatality rate of 12–30%. In a retrospective cohort of 120 SFTS patients (4 asymptomatic, 70 mild, 26 moderate, 20 severe), 17 (14.2%) had critical illness, of whom 11 died in-hospital (9.2%). Admission interleukin-6 (IL-6) rose across severity grades (mild 9.1, moderate 12.6, severe 61.4 pg/mL; p < 0.001) and was higher in critical illness than non-critical illness (99.4 vs. 10.0 pg/mL; p < 0.001). Critical illness patients had lower initial CD4 + T-cell counts (167 vs. 420 cells/μL; n = 63; p = 0.036) and a lower one-week CD4/CD8 ratio (0.5 vs. 1.6; n = 24; p = 0.0004). analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to investigate the immune response and interleukin-6 (IL-6) dynamics in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) to understand factors associated with critical illness and mortality.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 120 SFTS patients, stratified into asymptomatic, mild, moderate, and severe categories, with 17 patients experiencing critical illness.
analysis.methods: The study used mixed-effects models to analyze lymphocyte-fraction and platelet trajectories by outcome, and assessed admission IL-6 levels as a discriminatory marker.
analysis.main_results: Admission IL-6 levels increased with disease severity, reaching 61.4 pg/mL in severe cases (p < 0.001). Critical illness patients had lower initial CD4 + T-cell counts (167 vs. 420 cells/μL; p = 0.036) and a lower one-week CD4/CD8 ratio (0.5 vs.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that initial viral burden, rather than delayed clearance, is associated with critical illness, and that IL-6 levels may serve as a biomarker for severe disease.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results may inform the development of targeted diagnostic tools and therapeutic strategies for SFTS, particularly in identifying patients at risk of critical illness.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its retrospective design, and while IL-6 showed potential as a biomarker, its adjusted odds ratio was not significant. The evidence is moderate in strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study examines the immune response and interleukin-6 (IL-6) dynamics in severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (SFTS) to identify factors linked to critical illness and mortality. A retrospective cohort of 120 SFTS patients was stratified by disease severity, revealing that 14.2% experienced critical illness, with 9.2% dying in-hospital. Admission IL-6 levels were significantly higher in severe cases, and critical illness patients had lower initial CD4 + T-cell counts and a reduced CD4/CD8 ratio. Mixed-effects models showed distinct lymphocyte and platelet trajectories by outcome, and IL-6 was found to be a potential biomarker for severe disease. However, the study's retrospective nature and the non-significant adjusted odds ratio for IL-6 limit the strength of these findings, which are considered hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

papers.title: Epidemiological characteristics and recorded case fatality across prevention and control phases of SFTS in Changqing District, China, 2020–2025
papers.abstract: Objective This study aims to analyze the epidemiological characteristics, clinical diagnosis and treatment delays, and temporal changes in recorded case fatality and Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome (SFTS) -related knowledge across prevention and control phases for SFTS in Changqing District, Jinan City, from 2020 to 2025. The findings may inform local SFTS surveillance and prevention planning. Methods Data were collected from 119 laboratory-confirmed SFTS cases recorded between January 2020 and December 2025 in the Changqing District SFTS surveillance database, which was derived from the China National Notifiable Infectious Disease Surveillance System (NNIDSS). Descriptive epidemiological methods were employed to analyze temporal, spatial, and population distribution patterns. Additionally, questionnaire surveys evaluated changes in awareness of prevention measures among residents and healthcare workers before and after implementation of interventions. Annual and phase-specific CFRs were calculated with Wilson 95% confidence intervals. Recorded CFRs were compared across phases using the two-sided Fisher–Freeman–Halton exact test, and an exact ordinal trend test assessed trends across the three ordered phases. Unadjusted risk differences and risk ratios were reported with 95% confidence intervals. Annual incidence and recorded mortality trends were assessed using population-offset Poisson models, with assessment of overdispersion. Results The mean annual incidence rate was 3.27 per 100,000 population, with annual rates ranging from 1.50 to 4.74 per 100,000. Cases were reported from all townships and subdistricts. The highest estimated mean annual incidence rates were observed in Mashan Town (15.92 per 100,000), Shuangquan Town (12.57 per 100,000), and Xiaoli Town (8.68 per 100,000). Among recorded cases, the largest age group was 60–69 years (40.34%), and 86.55% were farmers (103/119). The median duration from symptom onset to diagnosis was 7 days, compared with a median interval of 1 day from symptom onset to first medical consultation. A substantial 61.34% of patients initially sought care at village clinics or township health centers. Annual recorded CFRs ranged from 6.90% (95% CI: 1.91%–21.96%) to 33.33% (95% CI: 12.06%–64.58%). Phase-specific recorded CFRs were 22.22%, 8.70%, and 20.83%, respectively, with no statistically significant difference among phases ( P = 0.416). The percentage of correct responses in the basic knowledge domain increased from 43.0% to 94.0% among residents and from 76.0% to 100.0% among healthcare workers between the pre-early-screening and comprehensive prevention and control phases. Conclusion Recorded SFTS cases in Changqing District showed geographical variation in estimated incidence, with farmers accounting for most cases and adults aged 60–69 years comprising the largest age group. Delays between symptom onset and diagnosis were observed. Recorded CFRs did not show a statistically significant or sustained decline across the prevention and control phases. These descriptive findings may inform surveillance and prevention planning.

papers.title: Burden of small-mammal-associated zoonoses in north-east Asia: A systematic review
papers.abstract: Small-mammal-associated zoonoses such as haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome, scrub typhus, leptospirosis and severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome are common notifiable infections in north-east Asia, but their burden in the region is poorly understood. Human cases are counted by separate surveillance systems with different case definitions, while infection in the small mammals and ectoparasites that maintain these pathogens is reported in a largely separate literature. The two are rarely measured in the same place and period, and the inputs a burden estimate needs are not reported consistently. This systematic review brings the two together for pathogens grouped into five transmission guilds. For the Republic of Korea, we extract all reported human, host and vector estimates for the four guilds other than flea-borne pathogens, and pool prevalence where studies are comparable. For the rest of north-east Asia (China, Japan, Mongolia, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, Taiwan and the Russian Far East), we map the available evidence for all five guilds without pooling. For each pathogen and country or area, we record which burden inputs are reported and which are missing. We also describe studies that measured infection in animals and disease in people in the same area. The expected outputs are pooled prevalence estimates for the Republic of Korea, an evidence map for the rest of the region, an inventory of missing burden inputs, and a minimum set of reporting items for future studies. The review is a first step towards a regional burden estimate.

The expected outputs are pooled prevalence estimates for the Republic of Korea, an evidence map for the rest of the region, an inventory of missing burden inputs, and a minimum set of reporting items for future studies. The review is a first step towards a regional burden estimate.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 本次综述聚焦于发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒)及其相关疾病的负担。其目标是评估发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒的流行病学影响,包括其传播动态、宿主范围以及疾病表现,同时考虑整合人类和动物监测数据的挑战。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本次综述是对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒及相关病原体现有文献的系统分析。它包括来自监测系统的数据以及关于小型哺乳动物和外寄生虫的研究数据。本次综述未进行元分析,而是对该地区的现有证据进行了映射,突出了数据收集和报告中的不一致性。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 综述得出结论,人类发热伴血小板减少综合征病例通过不同的监测系统进行报告,而小型哺乳动物和外寄生虫的感染情况则主要记录在另一套独立的文献中。这种缺乏整合导致了在该地区估算发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒真实负担的困难。综述还强调了结合人类和动物数据对于全面理解疾病的重要性。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 在不同研究和地区中,关于负担输入(如患病率和发病率)的报告缺乏一致性。此外,综述指出,关于发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒及相关病原体的数据往往是零散的,人类和动物研究之间存在有限的重叠。这导致了证据缺口,特别是在大韩民国以外的地区,由于无法进行汇总估算,因此难以获得全面的负担数据。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 综述强调了标准化监测和报告方法的必要性,以提高对发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒负担估算的准确性。它还建议未来的研究应整合人类和动物感染的数据,以更好地理解传播动态和疾病负担。此外,它呼吁制定最小报告项目集,以确保研究和监测工作的数据一致性。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Links SFTS Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical Treatment Hurdles by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Review Links SFTS Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical Treatment Hurdles Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scientific review published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology synthesizes the growing clinical, mechanistic, and translational findings on severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus, officially classified as Dabie bandavirus. First isolated in Henan Province in 2009, this tick-borne pathogen in the genus Bandavirus, family Phenuiviridae, represents an emerging public health threat across East and Southeast Asia. National epidemiological surveillance in China from 2010 to 2023, encompassing 27,447 confirmed cases, documented an overall case fatality rate of 4.83 percent, which decreased from 12.68 percent in 2010 to 3.77 percent in 2023. However, hospital cohorts enrolling severely ill patients report substantially higher case fatality rates ranging between 12 percent and 30 percent, with intensive care mortality reaching 50 percent. Designated a priority pathogen by the World Health Organization since 2017, the virus presents a widening gap between mechanistic understanding and clinical translation, driven by its systematic dismantling of host antiviral immune pathways. The transmission ecology and geographic distribution of the virus emphasize its capacity for broader international expansion beyond recognized endemic zones. The Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, serves as the primary vector and reservoir host, demonstrating viral persistence across larvae, nymphs, and adult stages. Surveillance across central and eastern China has revealed minimum tick infection rates of 0.17 percent and pool-positive rates reaching 20.0 percent, supported by transstadial and transovarial transmission. Other tick species, including Rhipicephalus microplus, Ixodes nipponensis, and Amblyomma testudinarium, also transmit the pathogen. The detection of Haemaphysalis longicornis in the United States highlights risks of international spread. Human cases occur across China, Japan, and South Korea, with serological or animal evidence identified in Vietnam, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar. Beyond tick bites, human-to-human transmission occurs through direct blood or fluid contact. A 2023 outbreak investigation in Zhejiang Province confirmed that seven of twelve cases contracted infection through direct blood exposure to a severely ill patient. Discover more Track Biotech Tour Colleges Cancer research funding The virion is an enveloped sphere measuring 80 to 120 nanometers containing three negative-sense or ambisense single-stranded RNA segments. The large segment of roughly 6,368 base pairs encodes the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase necessary for viral transcription and replication. The medium segment spans 3,378 base pairs encoding glycoprotein precursors cleaved into Gn and Gc, which mediate cellular attachment and membrane fusion. The ambisense small segment contains 1,746 base pairs, encoding nucleoprotein NP from antisense RNA and non-structural protein NSs from sense RNA. Cellular entry proceeds through clathrin-dependent endocytosis requiring an acidic endosomal environment and host cellular serine proteases. Multiple host receptors dictate cellular entry. DC-SIGN serves as a primary receptor on dendritic cells and macrophages, influencing the infection of plasmablasts. CRISPR-Cas9 screening identified chemokine receptor CCR2 as a key entry receptor binding Gn, with primary monocytes from elderly or diabetic patients showing elevated surface expression. Furthermore, knockout screening identified lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1, LRP1, as another conserved entry receptor mediating infection. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering The severity of infection reflects a sophisticated molecular strategy designed to paralyze host innate immune defenses. Non-structural protein NSs plays a central role by assembling viroplasm-like structures that sequester key signaling components of the type I interferon pathway, including RIG-I, TRIM25, TBK1, IKK-epsilon, and IRF3. Direct binding and sequestration of TRIM25 and TBK1 by NSs prevent IRF3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, thereby blocking interferon-beta transcription. Concurrently, NSs sequesters STAT2 and STAT1 into inclusion bodies, inhibiting downstream JAK-STAT signaling induced by interferons. The viral nucleoprotein NP reinforces this innate suppression through complementary mechanisms. NP promotes the autophagic degradation of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase by linking cGAS to autophagosome protein LC3. Additionally, NP triggers TUFM-dependent mitophagy to degrade mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein MAVS. By disrupting both cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS degradation and RNA sensing through MAVS clearance, the virus disables early intracellular defenses, facilitating unchecked viral replication throughout host tissues. Alongside innate suppression, the virus severely disrupts humoral and cellular adaptive immunity. The pathogen displays a pronounced tropism for monocytes and B cells, with differentiated plasma cells acting as primary viral reservoirs exhibiting marked downregulation of the interferon pathway. Fatal infections are characterized by a failure to produce neutralizing antibodies against glycoproteins Gn and NP, indicating extensive B-cell impairment. Early monocyte apoptosis diminishes antigen presentation by dendritic cells, hindering the activation of T follicular helper cells and undermining humoral responses. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses demonstrate that circulating T lymphocytes undergo quantitative depletion and functional exhaustion, with diminished cytotoxicity correlating strongly with patient mortality. Furthermore, alterations in natural killer cell activation and macrophage polarization impair coordinated host defense. This multifaceted disruption creates a paradoxical immunological state of profound immunosuppression coupled with persistent inflammation, rendering patients incapable of mounting protective antibody responses or clearing systemic viral loads. Simultaneously, severe infection triggers a dysregulated systemic cytokine storm characterized by elevated pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory mediators. Hospitalized patients display markedly increased circulating levels of interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-6, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor alpha, interferon gamma, IP-10, MIP-1 alpha, and MCP-1. Disease severity correlates positively with concentrations of interleukin-6, IP-10, and MCP-1, while both interleukin-6 and immunosuppressive interleukin-10 remain elevated until death in fatal cases. A critical driver of this hyperinflammation is the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. Infection induces overexpression of Bak and activates Bax, precipitating mitochondrial DNA oxidation and subsequent cytosolic release. Cytosolic oxidized mitochondrial DNA binds to and activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, which triggers Caspase-1 activation. Catalytically active Caspase-1 cleaves pro-interleukin-1 beta and pro-interleukin-18 into mature pro-inflammatory cytokines. Monocytes and macrophages serve as primary sources of these inflammatory mediators, driving widespread vascular leakage, high fever, and tissue pathology throughout disease progression. Pathological examinations in fatal cases demonstrate extensive cellular destruction across vital organs. Liver tissue exhibits hepatocyte necrosis and macrophage infiltration, kidney tissue reveals mononuclear infiltration around glomeruli, and lung tissue shows alveolar rupture with inflammatory invasion. Bone marrow evaluations reveal hemophagocytosis and histiocytic hyperplasia, with severe cases progressing to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Antiviral therapeutic options remain exceedingly limited, with significant hurdles restricting clinical efficacy. The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase inhibitor favipiravir was approved in Japan in June 2024 as the sole authorized antiviral for the disease. However, approval was granted based on a single-arm trial comparing results with historical controls rather than a randomized study. A randomized controlled trial by Li and colleagues reported overall mortality of 9.5 percent in favipiravir recipients compared to 18.3 percent in controls. Crucially, subgroup analyses demonstrated that therapeutic benefit was confined entirely to patients with low baseline viral loads exhibiting cycle threshold values of 26 or greater, where mortality fell from 11.5 percent to 1.6 percent. Favipiravir showed no significant benefit in patients with high viral loads or delayed therapy initiation. Other agents have yielded poor clinical translation; ribavirin demonstrated in vitro inhibition but failed to reduce mortality in a clinical study of 311 patients. Preclinical candidates such as VV251, an oral prodrug of 4′-fluorouridine, showed complete protection in lethal rodent models with substantially greater potency than favipiravir. Supportive clinical management remains the cornerstone of patient care, primarily involving fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, organ monitoring, and multiorgan support including mechanical ventilation and renal replacement therapy. Platelet and blood transfusions are frequently necessary to manage severe thrombocytopenia and acute hemorrhage. Controlling secondary coinfections is paramount; a multicenter study of 1,675 patients revealed that concurrent bacterial or fungal infections increased mortality from 6.7 percent to 24.3 percent. Corticosteroid use remains intensely debated, as immunosuppression can impede viral clearance and increase secondary infection risks, although co-administration with human albumin significantly lowered coinfection risks and improved clinical outcomes. Human cases occur across China, Japan, and South Korea, with serological or animal evidence identified in Vietnam, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar. A 2023 outbreak investigation in Zhejiang Province confirmed that seven of twelve cases contracted infection through direct blood exposure to a severely ill patient. analysis.brief_en: A scientific review published on November 18, 2026, in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology links the immune evasion mechanisms of the SFTS virus to clinical treatment challenges. The virus, classified as Dabie bandavirus, is a tick-borne pathogen first identified in Henan Province in 2009. National surveillance in China from 2010 to 2023 documented 27,447 confirmed cases with an overall case fatality rate of 4.83 percent, which has decreased over time. However, hospital cohorts of severely ill patients report fatality rates between 12 percent and 30 percent, with intensive care mortality reaching 50 percent. The review highlights the virus's ability to disrupt host immune pathways, including the type I interferon pathway and adaptive immunity, leading to severe disease outcomes. The virus is designated a priority pathogen by the World Health Organization since 2017, and its potential for international spread is underscored by the detection of its primary vector, the Asian longhorned tick, in the United States. The study also notes that human-to-human transmission occurs through direct blood or fluid contact, as evidenced by a 2023 outbreak in Zhejiang Province where seven of twelve cases were linked to such exposure. The findings emphasize the need for improved clinical translation and the exploration of novel immunomodulatory treatments, such as Janus kinase inhibitors and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, to address the virus's complex immune evasion strategies.

news.title_zh: Review Links 发热伴血小板减少综合征 Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical 治疗 Hurdles - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: A scientific review published on November 18, 2026, in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology links the immune evasion mechanisms of the SFTS virus to clinical treatment challenges. The virus, classified as Dabie bandavirus, is a tick-borne pathogen first identified in Henan Province in 2009. National surveillance in China from 2010 to 2023 documented 27,447 confirmed cases with an overall case fatality rate of 4.83 percent, which has decreased over time. However, hospital cohorts of severely ill patients report fatality rates between 12 percent and 30 percent, with intensive care mortality reaching 50 percent. The review highlights the virus's ability to disrupt host immune pathways, including the type I interferon pathway and adaptive immunity, leading to severe disease outcomes. The virus is designated a priority pathogen by the World Health Organization since 2017, and its potential for international spread is underscored by the detection of its primary vector, the Asian longhorned tick, in the United States. The study also notes that human-to-human transmission occurs through direct blood or fluid contact, as evidenced by a 2023 outbreak in Zhejiang Province where seven of twelve cases were linked to such exposure. The findings emphasize the need for improved clinical translation and the exploration of novel immunomodulatory treatments, such as Janus kinase inhibitors and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, to address the virus's complex immune evasion strategies.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Dabie Bandavirus Fatality Linked to Genotype B in Coastal East Asia by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Dabie Bandavirus Fatality Linked to Genotype B in Coastal East Asia Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, an emerging tick-borne zoonosis caused by Dabie bandavirus, exhibits a pronounced epidemiological decoupling between infection frequency and clinical severity across mainland China. A comprehensive investigation integrating nationwide epidemiological surveillance, multi-center hospital cohorts, and large-scale viral genomics has identified an unexpected geographic divergence characterized as an inland-high-incidence versus coastal-high-fatality paradox. Between 2010 and 2023, Chinese national public health surveillance recorded 27,457 cases of the disease and 1,326 related deaths across 27 provinces and municipalities. Strikingly, spatial analysis demonstrated that transmission was overwhelmingly concentrated within seven core provinces, accounting for 99.05 percent of all reported incident infections and 99.62 percent of total recorded fatalities. Rather than displaying uniform clinical outcomes across this endemic belt, the disease presented two fundamentally distinct operational profiles. Inland provinces recorded high case volumes with comparatively low mortality, whereas maritime coastal jurisdictions experienced significantly fewer infections but suffered disproportionately severe clinical outcomes. This observed geographic divergence challenges traditional uniform surveillance models and underscores the complex interplay among viral genetics, local ecology, and regional transmission dynamics. Rigorous statistical comparison between inland provinces, comprising Henan, Hubei, and Anhui, and coastal provinces, including Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, and Liaoning, confirmed this stark epidemiological decoupling. Inland jurisdictions exhibited a combined cumulative incidence rate of 7.31 cases per 100,000 population, whereas coastal provinces recorded a substantially lower cumulative incidence rate of 3.84 cases per 100,000 population. When using the inland zone as the baseline epidemiological reference, the relative risk of acquiring an infection in coastal regions was calculated at 0.52. Conversely, case fatality rates exhibited the exact inverse trajectory between these geographic zones. The recorded case fatality rate across inland provinces was 2.61 percent, compared to 8.04 percent in coastal regions, representing a 3.08-fold elevated risk of fatal outcome for coastal patients. At the individual provincial level, this contrast was exemplified by comparing Henan and Zhejiang. Discover more Track Biotech Tour Colleges Cancer research funding To uncover the ecological drivers shaping regional transmission patterns, researchers evaluated environmental datasets spanning 2012 through 2018 using generalized additive models with an incorporated one-month time lag. Analyses focused on Xinyang in inland Henan and Zhoushan in coastal Zhejiang to quantify how ambient temperature, precipitation, and sunshine duration modulate human infection risk. The empirical modeling demonstrated that viral transmission consistently lagged ambient temperature increases by one month, corresponding to the biological interval necessary for tick vector activation and viral propagation. In inland Xinyang, transmission dynamics showed extreme climatic vulnerability, with relative risk escalating sharply once ambient temperatures crossed a 10-degree Celsius threshold, reaching peak sensitivity at 20.6 degrees Celsius with a relative risk of 4.85. Coastal Zhoushan exhibited a moderated temperature response, peaking at 22.6 degrees Celsius with a relative risk of 3.07. Crucially, coastal environments revealed a distinct meteorological threshold effect where monthly sunshine duration exceeding 200 hours triggered precipitous increases in relative risk. Overall, meteorological variables explained 82.1 percent of incidence variance in Xinyang compared to only 48.7 percent in Zhoushan, confirming climate-buffered coastal transmission. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering Genomic characterization of 1,820 curated viral genomes from China, Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Thailand revealed that regional clinical disparities closely align with geographic viral lineage structures. Dabie bandavirus possesses a tripartite negative-sense RNA genome consisting of Large, Medium, and Small segments that encode essential replication enzymes, envelope glycoproteins, and structural proteins. Phylogenetic reconstruction and multidimensional scaling across all three genomic segments consistently resolved five major clades, officially designated as genotypes A through E. Hierarchical clustering based on regional genotypic compositions separated the sampled geographic areas into two distinct major clades. Inland Chinese provinces clustered together into a clade dominated by high frequencies of genotype C, alongside co-circulating genotypes A and D. In contrast, coastal Zhejiang clustered directly with Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Thailand into a lineage group dominated almost exclusively by genotype B. This distinct spatial segregation established that coastal populations in East Asia are exposed to an entirely different viral population structure than patients infected across inland agricultural regions. High-resolution phylogeographic mapping within the coastal and insular environments of Zhejiang province demonstrated profound evolutionary compartmentalization that defies traditional continuous diffusion models. Despite close administrative proximity, viral populations circulating in Xiangshan county and Ningbo urban center followed completely separate micro-evolutionary paths. Constrained by its peninsular geography and active deepwater port facilities, Xiangshan harbored a highly conserved, sequestered genotype B subclade, illustrating a classic peninsular evolutionary effect where marine isolation filters gene flow. Conversely, urban Ningbo maintained broader genetic diversity comprising genotypes A, B, and C with evident mainland affinities. Across the Zhoushan archipelago, Shengsi island harbored a genotype B sublineage genetically closer to Japanese isolates than to those circulating on adjacent domestic islands, while neighboring Qushan island was dominated by genotype A lineages aligned with northern Shandong strains. Isolation-by-distance regression analysis confirmed negligible spatial correlation across these island locations, proving that geographic distance fails to predict genetic divergence in fragmented marine settings where maritime transport and discontinuous physical barriers dominate over gradual terrestrial dispersal. Genomic screening across the curated isolate dataset revealed that Zhejiang functions as an active geographic crossroads for viral reassortment and genetic recombination. The overall reassortment frequency among the 1,820 analyzed strains was 4.1 percent, characterized by discordance among the genotypes assigned to the Large, Medium, and Small segments. In Zhejiang, predominant reassortant constellations included configurations B-A-B and D-C-D, whereas Henan strains predominantly displayed mixed combinations of genotypes A, C, and D. Recombination analyses across individual genomic segments detected events in 2.6 percent of Large segments, 1.8 percent of Medium segments, and 0.4 percent of Small segments. Notably, viral isolates from coastal Zhejiang exhibited a recombination frequency of 11.0 percent, which was significantly higher than the 3.5 percent observed in inland Henan and the 3.9 percent identified in the Republic of Korea. Directional parental mapping confirmed that Zhejiang recombinants derived genomic material from diverse domestic and international lineages, indicating that coastal ecological interfaces provide fertile evolutionary ground for the emergence of novel viral variants. Discrete Bayesian phylogeographic modeling of Small-segment sequences from Zhejiang, the Republic of Korea, and Japan reconstructed complex trans-oceanic dispersal pathways operating across East Asia. The molecular clock analysis yielded a mean evolutionary substitution rate of 9.37 multiplied by 10 to the negative fifth power substitutions per site per year, placing the time to the most recent common ancestor around the year 1697. Ancestral state reconstruction supported a polyphyletic origin, identifying Hangzhou, the Republic of Korea, and Japan as supported root locations. Spatial transition matrices identified robust cross-border transmission pathways connecting the Republic of Korea to both Japanese prefectures and coastal Zhejiang centers, accompanied by counter-directional lineage seeding from Zhejiang back to the Korean peninsula. Domestically, the model detected active viral exchanges between offshore islands and mainland cities, including dispersal routes from Daishan island into Taizhou and Huzhou. These maritime transmission corridors overlap with the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, where millions of migratory shorebirds regularly transport parasitizing Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks across open maritime straits during seasonal migration. Clinical comparisons between 805 laboratory-confirmed patients in Henan and 131 patients in Zhejiang provided direct evidence linking specific viral lineages to patient outcomes. While both cohorts shared comparable demographic age and sex distributions, patients in coastal Zhejiang experienced significantly longer intervals between initial symptom onset and hospital admission, accompanied by higher clinical mortality. In the Henan cohort, genotype D infection was associated with a case fatality rate of 26.1 percent, significantly exceeding the mortality observed for genotype A at 14.4 percent and genotype C at 15.6 percent. Molecular evolutionary analysis uncovered critical adaptive signatures and specific amino acid markers that correlate with the heightened lethality of coastal infections. Selection pressure evaluations using codon-aware alignments demonstrated elevated ratios of non-synonymous to synonymous substitutions within the non-structural proteins and glycoprotein Gn of genotype B, indicating episodic positive selection or relaxed purifying pressure during viral adaptation. Genetic association models identified the RdRp-N828S substitution, located within the viral polymerase finger subdomain, as an independent molecular predictor of fatal clinical outcome, conferring an adjusted odds ratio of 2.52. Conversely, the genotype B-specific substitution RdRp-A1433T was significantly associated with reduced mortality risk, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 0.47. In addition to these functional polymerase alterations, multiple conserved structural markers, including NP-R52, Gn-S501, Gn-S218, Gc-S449, and Gc-S100, were present in over 90 percent of genotype B isolates while appearing in fewer than 10 percent of other lineages, providing definitive diagnostic targets for high-virulence genomic screening. The authors emphasized several methodological and biological caveats regarding the interpretation of these regional findings. The associations identified between specific viral genotypes, amino acid substitutions, and clinical fatality remain observational and require definitive functional validation through reverse genetics and experimental animal challenge models. Furthermore, ecological modeling relied on macro-meteorological measurements that cannot capture localized micro-environmental variables such as tick habitat density, vegetation indices, or domestic host abundance. In addition, the proposed dissemination of viral lineages via migratory birds along maritime flyways represents an epidemiologically sound hypothesis that requires direct verification through longitudinal tick screening at avian stopover sites. Finally, the statistical power of the genotype-specific survival analyses within Zhejiang was constrained by a relatively small sequenced clinical cohort compared to Henan. Despite these limitations, the evidence demonstrates that public health frameworks must transition away from uniform national guidelines toward genotype-informed precision surveillance, implementing tailored seasonal interventions across inland regions while prioritizing persistent vector management in high-fatality coastal corridors. news.source_body_en: A study in China identified a significant geographic divergence in the transmission and clinical outcomes of Dabie bandavirus. Inland provinces experienced high case volumes with low mortality, while coastal regions had fewer infections but higher fatality rates. The study highlighted the role of climate and viral genotypes in transmission dynamics, but further investigation is required to understand the underlying mechanisms.
news.content_zh: 一项在中国进行的研究发现,大别山布尼亚病毒在传播和临床结果方面存在显著的地理差异。内陆省份感染病例数量高但死亡率较低,而沿海地区感染病例较少但致死率较高。该研究强调了气候和病毒基因型在传播动态中的作用,但需要进一步研究以理解其潜在机制。

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Machine Learning Model Predicts In-Hospital Mortality in Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome by November 14, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Machine Learning Model Predicts In-Hospital Mortality in Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram An explainable machine learning model integrating viral, immune, and inflammatory biomarkers can predict in-hospital mortality among patients diagnosed with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, according to a study published in BMC Infectious Diseases. Researchers established that a final logistic regression model based on four biological indicators achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.841 in an internal validation cohort. The predictive framework was constructed to identify patients facing elevated mortality risks during hospitalization while maintaining individual interpretability through feature attribution methods. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome is characterized by an excessive inflammatory response and impaired adaptive immunity, carrying a substantial risk of patient mortality. The study aimed to establish and validate a machine learning-based predictive model integrating clinical and immune-inflammatory biomarkers for in-hospital mortality in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. The investigation evaluated clinical data from a total of 238 patients diagnosed with the syndrome, comprising 177 survivors and 61 non-survivors. To train and evaluate the predictive algorithms without information leakage, the cohort was divided through stratified random sampling at a seven-to-three ratio. This split allocated 167 patients to the primary training cohort and reserved the remaining 71 patients for an independent internal validation cohort dedicated exclusively to final model testing. Discover more Machine Learning Learn AI Tools machine learning Machine learning Find Treatments Candidate predictor variables were isolated using an intersection of three distinct computational screening techniques: the Boruta algorithm, the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, and random forest recursive feature elimination. All algorithm hyperparameters were optimized exclusively within the training cohort using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. To demystify the internal decision-making mechanics of the resulting models, investigators applied SHapley Additive exPlanations, providing clear interpretability for the relative contribution of each selected biological feature. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Scoping Review Identifies Broad Animal Hosts Driving Severe Fever With Thrombocytopenia Virus by November 17, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Scoping Review Identifies Broad Animal Hosts Driving Severe Fever With Thrombocytopenia Virus Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scoping review synthesizing evidence across 353 published studies has mapped the extensive vertebrate host networks that maintain and transmit severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, widely known as SFTS, is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis caused by a member of the genus Bandavirus within the family Phenuiviridae. First recognized in China in 2009, the viral pathogen has expanded its known geographic footprint across East Asia, including Japan and the Republic of Korea, with subsequent detections recorded in Southeast Asia. In human patients, infection triggers an acute febrile illness accompanied by severe thrombocytopenia, leukocytopenia, and gastrointestinal symptoms, which can rapidly progress to multiorgan dysfunction and hemorrhagic complications. Case-fatality ratios among clinical human cases range between 5 percent and 30 percent, with the greatest mortality observed in older adults and patients experiencing comorbid health conditions. Because viral persistence depends entirely on complex ecological cycles linking vertebrate animal hosts and hematophagous ticks, researchers conducted this systematic synthesis to clarify cross-species dynamics under an integrated One Health framework. To rigorously chart how vertebrate hosts contribute to disease maintenance and zoonotic spillover, the research team designed an exhaustive scoping review in full accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. The authors systematically searched major electronic databases, specifically querying PubMed and MEDLINE alongside prominent Chinese bibliographic databases including the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals. The literature search window spanned records published from January 1, 2011 through October 21, 2025, capturing findings established since the initial identification of the disease. The bibliographic retrieval yielded 2180 candidate records, comprising 191 from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, 1591 from Wanfang Data, 262 from the VIP database, and 136 from PubMed. After screening titles and abstracts, removing 132 duplicate citations, and retrieving 1680 full-text reports, the investigators identified 353 eligible investigations that met all inclusion criteria for qualitative, narrative, and thematic synthesis across predetermined ecological and clinical domains. The synthesized evidence reveals that the pathogen circulates across an exceptionally broad vertebrate spectrum involving at least 15 animal species spanning domestic livestock, peri-domestic mammals, free-roaming wildlife, and household companion animals. Domestic livestock serve as vital amplification hosts capable of supporting high seroprevalence rates across endemic rural agricultural zones. A referenced meta-analysis estimated pooled seroprevalence at 45.7 percent in sheep and goats and 36.7 percent in domestic cattle, alongside lower yet measurable seroprevalence levels in domestic pigs and chickens. Although active viremia in domestic ruminants appears relatively transient, resulting in significantly lower molecular polymerase chain reaction positivity rates than antibody detection rates, both viral ribonucleic acid detection and successful viral isolation confirm active replication. Pasture access, free-range grazing management, and local tick density directly correlate with elevated livestock seropositivity. At the village level in endemic areas, SFTSV ribonucleic acid prevalence detected in domestic livestock consistently exceeds the infection rates identified in questing ticks or surveyed human populations. The principal vector sustaining viral transmission across endemic ecosystems is the hematophagous tick Haemaphysalis longicornis. Both field surveys and laboratory experiments demonstrate that this tick species acquires the virus during blood feeding on viremic vertebrate hosts and maintains infection transstadially across life stages as well as transovarially through maternal egg transmission. Additional vector species, including Haemaphysalis flava, Ixodes sinensis, and Rhipicephalus sanguineus, have also tested positive for viral genetic material, indicating potential multi-vector maintenance in distinct ecologies. In controlled laboratory trials, ticks feeding on infected laboratory mice successfully acquired the virus, survived developmental molting, passed the infection to offspring, and subsequently inoculated naive mice during subsequent blood meals. Natural livestock exposure mirrors this vector dependency: when naive sentinel goats were experimentally housed in endemic pastures, they acquired infection shortly following heavy tick infestation. Furthermore, molecular sequencing revealed that viral isolates obtained from naturally infected goat serum and the ticks feeding upon them shared 100 percent nucleotide sequence homology across the viral S-segment. Free-roaming and peri-domestic wildlife contribute essential redundancy to natural sylvatic maintenance cycles across fragmented landscapes. Documented infections and antibody seropositivity have been verified in diverse wild species, including wild boar, hedgehogs, shrews, and small rodents. Because small mammals routinely host immature nymphal and larval stages of Haemaphysalis ticks, these species likely drive seasonal maintenance cycles and local geographic clustering. However, the review emphasizes that existing wildlife evidence stems primarily from observational serology or ribonucleic acid detection rather than controlled host-competence experiments. Consequently, the exact duration of wildlife viremia and the efficiency of transmission to feeding ticks remain incompletely defined. In contrast, captive fur-bearing animals represent an intensive, high-density production interface. An investigated outbreak on a mink farm in Weihai, China, documented two human cases where genomic analysis demonstrated 99.9 percent sequence homology between viral strains recovered from infected farm workers, captive mink, and environmental swabs, indicating potential transmission via aerosols generated during animal skinning or through direct contact with blood and visceral tissues. Clinical manifestations of infection diverge drastically across vertebrate species, illustrating stark biological gradients in tissue tropism and immune restriction. While domestic ruminants and livestock typically endure subclinical or remarkably mild infections without overt morbidity, domestic felines exhibit extreme physiological vulnerability. Infected domestic cats frequently develop fulminant viral hemorrhagic fever characterized by sustained pyrexia, anorexia, severe cytopenias, macroscopic hemorrhages, and high case fatality. Histopathological examinations of diseased cats demonstrate severe necrotizing lymphadenitis and extensive hemophagocytosis, closely paralleling the fatal pathological progression observed in severe human cases. This shared immunopathology is driven by marked cytokine dysregulation, marked by substantial elevations in interferon-alpha, interferon-gamma, interleukin-6, interleukin-10, granulocyte-colony stimulating factor, and interferon gamma-induced protein 10. By comparison, domestic dogs typically display self-limiting fever and transient hematological abnormalities, recovering with standard supportive veterinary care, yet they uniquely demonstrate prolonged shedding of infectious viral particles in their urine long after apparent clinical resolution. Beyond classical vector inoculation through tick bites, direct non-vector animal-to-human transmission poses a documented and hazardous spillover pathway. Human infections, including fatal illness following cat bites or intensive nursing care of moribund pets without visible tick attachment, demonstrate the viability of contact and mucosal transmission routes. Canine urinary shedding similarly extends environmental exposure windows, while occupational serological screening among veterinary hospital workers in Japan confirmed detectable antibody prevalence among practicing clinicians and nurses. Transmission between animals has also been substantiated in controlled laboratory settings: infected ferrets shed high concentrations of viral ribonucleic acid through nasal discharge, saliva, and urine for up to 12 days, transmitting the pathogen to naive co-housed ferrets via direct contact and urine-contaminated fomites. Conversely, naive goats co-housed with infected goats without ticks did not contract infection, proving direct contact transmission does not readily occur within typical ruminant herds. Conversely, the scoping review uncovered no verifiable empirical evidence demonstrating human-to-animal transmission; while biologically plausible under intensive contact conditions, reverse zoonotic spillover currently remains entirely uninvestigated in the scientific literature. Because multiple transmission interfaces operate simultaneously across domestic, agricultural, and clinical environments, the review authors highlight that public health messaging focused solely on avoiding outdoor tick bites fails to capture the true spectrum of exposure risk encountered by pet owners, livestock handlers, and veterinary personnel. Translating these findings into effective disease control demands coordinated One Health interventions uniting chemical, environmental, and clinical biosecurity measures. Integrated tick management represents the primary operational barrier, combining routine acaricide treatments for livestock and companion animals with pasture perimeter mowing, vegetation clearance, and rotational grazing designed to disrupt tick microhabitats. In veterinary clinics and agricultural settings, strict biosecurity protocols must mandate personal protective equipment, including protective gloves, surgical masks, and eye protection, when handling febrile or clinically suspect felines and livestock. Although no antiviral therapeutics have gained regulatory approval for human SFTS, investigational favipiravir has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in animal models and advanced into clinical trials, while experimental monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral envelope glycoprotein Gn have exhibited protective neutralizing capacity in preclinical studies. Preventative vaccine pipelines encompass experimental live-attenuated, viral-vectored, and deoxyribonucleic acid candidates, alongside anti-tick vaccines designed to impair vector feeding mechanics and prospective veterinary vaccines formulated to suppress amplification in domestic livestock. The review concludes by outlining critical operational priorities required to transform descriptive ecological observations into predictive public health strategies. Future research must standardize longitudinal host-competence experiments to precisely quantify species-specific viremia curves and correlate them directly with empirical tick acquisition thresholds. Establishing harmonized, multispecies diagnostic panels with standardized cycle threshold criteria and plaque reduction neutralization test benchmarks across veterinary and public health laboratories is essential for accurate cross-species surveillance. Furthermore, implementation research must rigorously evaluate the feasibility, community acceptability, and cost-effectiveness of combined intervention bundles, including targeted veterinary vaccination of key amplifying species such as small ruminants, particularly across resource-constrained rural communities experiencing the greatest disease burden. Ultimately, mitigating severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome requires replacing fragmented, human-only outbreak responses with institutionalized, multi-sectoral surveillance systems that triangulate animal serological monitoring, vector density tracking, and environmental data to anticipate viral surges and proactively prevent zoonotic spillover. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, widely known as SFTS, is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis caused by a member of the genus Bandavirus within the family Phenuiviridae. First recognized in China in 2009, the viral pathogen has expanded its known geographic footprint across East Asia, including Japan and the Republic of Korea, with subsequent detections recorded in Southeast Asia. In human patients, infection triggers an acute febrile illness accompanied by severe thrombocytopenia, leukocytopenia, and gastrointestinal symptoms, which can rapidly progress to multiorgan dysfunction and hemorrhagic complications. Case-fatality ratios among clinical human cases range between 5 percent and 30 percent, with the greatest mortality observed in older adults and patients experiencing comorbid health conditions. Because viral persistence depends entirely on complex ecological cycles linking vertebrate animal hosts and hematophagous ticks, researchers conducted this systematic synthesis to clarify cross-species dynamics under an integrated One Health framework. To rigorously chart how vertebrate hosts contribute to disease maintenance and zoonotic spillover, the research team designed an exhaustive scoping review in full accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guidelines. The authors systematically searched major electronic databases, specifically querying PubMed and MEDLINE alongside prominent Chinese bibliographic databases including the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, Wanfang Data, and the VIP Database for Chinese Technical Periodicals. The literature search window spanned records published from January 1, 2011 through October 21, 2025, capturing findings established since the initial identification of the disease. The bibliographic retrieval yielded 2180 candidate records, comprising 191 from the China National Knowledge Infrastructure, 1591 from Wanfang Data, 262 from the VIP database, and 136 from PubMed. After screening titles and abstracts, removing 132 duplicate citations, and retrieving 1680 full-text reports, the investigators identified 353 eligible investigations that met all inclusion criteria for qualitative, narrative, and thematic synthesis across predetermined ecological and clinical domains. The synthesized evidence reveals that the pathogen circulates across an exceptionally broad vertebrate spectrum involving at least 15 animal species spanning domestic livestock, peri-domestic mammals, free-roaming wildlife, and household companion animals. Domestic livestock serve as vital amplification hosts capable of supporting high seroprevalence rates across endemic rural agricultural zones. A referenced meta-analysis estimated pooled seroprevalence at 45.7 percent in sheep and goats and 36.7 percent in domestic cattle, alongside lower yet measurable seroprevalence levels in domestic pigs and chickens. Although active viremia in domestic ruminants appears relatively transient, resulting in significantly lower molecular polymerase chain reaction positivity rates than antibody detection rates, both viral ribonucleic acid detection and successful viral isolation confirm active replication. Pasture access, free-range grazing management, and local tick density directly correlate with elevated livestock seropositivity. At the village level in endemic areas, SFTSV ribonucleic acid prevalence detected in domestic livestock consistently exceeds the infection rates identified in questing ticks or surveyed human populations. The principal vector sustaining viral transmission across endemic ecosystems is the hematophagous tick Haemaphysalis longicornis. Both field surveys and laboratory experiments demonstrate that this tick species acquires the virus during blood feeding on viremic vertebrate hosts and maintains infection transstadially across life stages as well as transovarially through maternal egg transmission. Additional vector species, including Haemaphysalis flava, Ixodes sinensis, and Rhipicephalus sanguineus, have also tested positive for viral genetic material, indicating potential multi-vector maintenance in distinct ecologies. In controlled laboratory trials, ticks feeding on infected laboratory mice successfully acquired the virus, survived developmental molting, passed the infection to offspring, and subsequently inoculated naive mice during subsequent blood meals. Natural livestock exposure mirrors this vector dependency: when naive sentinel goats were experimentally housed in endemic pastures, they acquired infection shortly following heavy tick infestation. Furthermore, molecular sequencing revealed that viral isolates obtained from naturally infected goat serum and the ticks feeding upon them shared 100 percent nucleotide sequence homology across the viral S-segment. Free-roaming and peri-domestic wildlife contribute essential redundancy to natural sylvatic maintenance cycles across fragmented landscapes. Documented infections and antibody seropositivity have been verified in diverse wild species, including wild boar, hedgehogs, shrews, and small rodents. Because small mammals routinely host immature nymphal and larval stages of Haemaphysalis ticks, these species likely drive seasonal maintenance cycles and local geographic clustering. However, the review emphasizes that existing wildlife evidence stems primarily from observational serology or ribonucleic acid detection rather than controlled host-competence experiments. Consequently, the exact duration of wildlife viremia and the efficiency of transmission to feeding ticks remain incompletely defined. In contrast, captive fur-bearing animals represent an intensive, high-density production interface. An investigated outbreak on a mink farm in Weihai, China, documented two human cases where genomic analysis demonstrated 99.9 percent sequence homology between viral strains recovered from infected farm workers, captive mink, and environmental swabs, indicating potential transmission via aerosols generated during animal skinning or through direct contact with blood and visceral tissues. Clinical manifestations of infection diverge drastically across vertebrate species, illustrating stark biological gradients in tissue tropism and immune restriction. While domestic ruminants and livestock typically endure subclinical or remarkably mild infections without overt morbidity, domestic felines exhibit extreme physiological vulnerability. Infected domestic cats frequently develop fulminant viral hemorrhagic fever characterized by sustained pyrexia, anorexia, severe cytopenias, macroscopic hemorrhages, and high case fatality. Histopathological examinations of diseased cats demonstrate severe necrotizing lymphadenitis and extensive hemophagocytosis, closely paralleling the fatal pathological progression observed in severe human cases. This shared immunopathology is driven by marked cytokine dysregulation, marked by substantial elevations in interferon-alpha, interferon-gamma, interleukin-6, interleukin-10, granulocyte-colony stimulating factor, and interferon gamma-induced protein 10. By comparison, domestic dogs typically display self-limiting fever and transient hematological abnormalities, recovering with standard supportive veterinary care, yet they uniquely demonstrate prolonged shedding of infectious viral particles in their urine long after apparent clinical resolution. Beyond classical vector inoculation through tick bites, direct non-vector animal-to-human transmission poses a documented and hazardous spillover pathway. Human infections, including fatal illness following cat bites or intensive nursing care of moribund pets without visible tick attachment, demonstrate the viability of contact and mucosal transmission routes. Canine urinary shedding similarly extends environmental exposure windows, while occupational serological screening among veterinary hospital workers in Japan confirmed detectable antibody prevalence among practicing clinicians and nurses. Transmission between animals has also been substantiated in controlled laboratory settings: infected ferrets shed high concentrations of viral ribonucleic acid through nasal discharge, saliva, and urine for up to 12 days, transmitting the pathogen to naive co-housed ferrets via direct contact and urine-contaminated fomites. Conversely, naive goats co-housed with infected goats without ticks did not contract infection, proving direct contact transmission does not readily occur within typical ruminant herds. Conversely, the scoping review uncovered no verifiable empirical evidence demonstrating human-to-animal transmission; while biologically plausible under intensive contact conditions, reverse zoonotic spillover currently remains entirely uninvestigated in the scientific literature. Because multiple transmission interfaces operate simultaneously across domestic, agricultural, and clinical environments, the review authors highlight that public health messaging focused solely on avoiding outdoor tick bites fails to capture the true spectrum of exposure risk encountered by pet owners, livestock handlers, and veterinary personnel. Translating these findings into effective disease control demands coordinated One Health interventions uniting chemical, environmental, and clinical biosecurity measures. Integrated tick management represents the primary operational barrier, combining routine acaricide treatments for livestock and companion animals with pasture perimeter mowing, vegetation clearance, and rotational grazing designed to disrupt tick microhabitats. In veterinary clinics and agricultural settings, strict biosecurity protocols must mandate personal protective equipment, including protective gloves, surgical masks, and eye protection, when handling febrile or clinically suspect felines and livestock. Although no antiviral therapeutics have gained regulatory approval for human SFTS, investigational favipiravir has demonstrated therapeutic efficacy in animal models and advanced into clinical trials, while experimental monoclonal antibodies targeting the viral envelope glycoprotein Gn have exhibited protective neutralizing capacity in preclinical studies. Preventative vaccine pipelines encompass experimental live-attenuated, viral-vectored, and deoxyribonucleic acid candidates, alongside anti-tick vaccines designed to impair vector feeding mechanics and prospective veterinary vaccines formulated to suppress amplification in domestic livestock. The review concludes by outlining critical operational priorities required to transform descriptive ecological observations into predictive public health strategies. Future research must standardize longitudinal host-competence experiments to precisely quantify species-specific viremia curves and correlate them directly with empirical tick acquisition thresholds. Establishing harmonized, multispecies diagnostic panels with standardized cycle threshold criteria and plaque reduction neutralization test benchmarks across veterinary and public health laboratories is essential for accurate cross-species surveillance. Furthermore, implementation research must rigorously evaluate the feasibility, community acceptability, and cost-effectiveness of combined intervention bundles, including targeted veterinary vaccination of key amplifying species such as small ruminants, particularly across resource-constrained rural communities experiencing the greatest disease burden. Ultimately, mitigating severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome requires replacing fragmented, human-only outbreak responses with institutionalized, multi-sectoral surveillance systems that triangulate animal serological monitoring, vector density tracking, and environmental data to anticipate viral surges and proactively prevent zoonotic spillover. analysis.brief_en: A scoping review of 353 studies has identified the broad range of vertebrate hosts that contribute to the maintenance and transmission of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV), including domestic livestock, peri-domestic mammals, free-roaming wildlife, and household companion animals. The review, published on November 17, 2026, highlights that SFTSV is an emerging tick-borne zoonosis, primarily transmitted by Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks, with additional vector species also implicated. The study found that domestic livestock, such as sheep, goats, and cattle, show high seroprevalence rates, and an outbreak on a mink farm in Weihai, China, linked two human cases to the virus, suggesting potential transmission via aerosols or direct contact with infected animals. Case-fatality ratios range from 5% to 30%, with higher mortality observed in older adults and those with comorbid conditions. The review emphasizes the need for comprehensive public health strategies that address multiple transmission routes, including those involving livestock handlers and pet owners, as current messaging often focuses solely on tick bites.
