The study found that domestic livestock, such as sheep, goats, and cattle, show high seroprevalence rates, and an outbreak on a mink farm in Weihai, China, linked two human cases to the virus, suggesting potential transmission via aerosols or direct contact with infected animals. Case-fatality ratios range from 5% to 30%, with higher mortality observed in older adults and those with comorbid conditions. The review emphasizes the need for comprehensive public health strategies that address multiple transmission routes, including those involving livestock handlers and pet owners, as current messaging often focuses solely on tick bites.
news.content_zh: 一项涵盖353项研究的范围综述确定了广泛参与严重发热伴血小板减少综合征病毒(SFTSV)维持和传播的脊椎动物宿主,包括家畜、家周哺乳动物、自由活动的野生动物以及家庭宠物。该综述于2026年11月17日发表,强调SFTSV是一种新兴的蜱媒 人兽共患病,主要通过长角血体螨(Haemaphysalis longicornis)传播,还有其他媒介物种也涉及其中。研究发现,家畜如羊、山羊和牛表现出高血清流行率率,并且在中国威海的一家貂养殖场发生的一起暴发中,发现了两例人类病例与该病毒有关,表明病毒可能通过气溶胶或直接接触感染动物的血液和组织传播。病例死亡率范围为5%至30%,老年人和有合并症的人群死亡率较高。综述强调需要制定全面的公共卫生策略,应对多种传播途径,包括涉及家畜处理者和宠物主人的途径,因为当前的信息传播往往仅关注蜱虫叮咬。

news.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ SYSTEM NOTICE Auto translation by AI. Be sure, accuracy, nuances and authorial intent may not be fully reflected. Show original Current Topics: Record High SFTS Cases! Beware of Transmission from Dogs and Cats to Humans! 研究所 Nov 14, 2026 12:45 In recent years, the number of patients with "SFTS (Severe Fever with Thrombocytopenia Syndrome)" has been increasing in Japan. In 2025, 191 patients were reported nationwide, marking a record high (provisional value). Previously, cases were mainly concentrated in western Japan, but infections are now being confirmed in eastern Japan as well, making it an infectious disease that requires caution. ■ What kind of disease is SFTS? SFTS virus is an infectious disease caused by the tick, and it is mainly transmitted through bites from infected ticks. When infected, symptoms such as fever, loss of appetite, vomiting, and diarrhea appear. Blood tests characteristically show a decrease in white blood cells and platelets. It can be fatal if it becomes severe, and the case fatality rate for patients in Japan is reported to be approximately 10–30%. ■ Can dogs and cats also get infected? Yes. Dogs and cats can also be infected with SFTS. Cats, in particular, are prone to severe illness, with domestic reports indicating a case fatality rate of approximately 60–70%. Even more importantly, it can be transmitted to humans through contact with the blood, saliva, etc., of infected cats and dogs. In fact, cases of infection among veterinary professionals such as veterinarians and veterinary nurses have been reported. ■ What should be kept in mind at veterinary clinics? When examining animals suspected of having SFTS, infection control measures are extremely important. ・Appropriately use gloves, masks, gowns, eye protection, etc. ・Avoid direct contact with blood, saliva, excrement, etc. ・Be careful of bites and scratches ・Properly clean and disinfect used instruments and examination tables ・Implement isolation and traffic line management for suspected cases ■ Key points to remember for the national examination 1 Pathogen: SFTS virus (Phenuiviridae family) 2 Main vector: Tick 3 Infected animals: Humans, dogs, cats, etc. 4 Main symptoms: Fever, loss of appetite, vomiting, diarrhea 5 Characteristic laboratory findings: Leukopenia and thrombocytopenia 6 Zoonotic disease, and there is also direct transmission from infected animals to humans 7 Under Japan's Infectious Diseases Control Law, it is a Category IV infectious disease 【Summary】 SFTS can be transmitted to humans not only by tick bites but also through contact with infected dogs and cats. For veterinary nurses, it is extremely important to understand not only the disease itself but also preventive measures to protect themselves from infection. According to the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's "SFTS Clinical Guidelines 2025," 194 cats and 12 dogs were reported to have developed the disease in Japan in 2024. It is clear that while it is a human infectious disease, it is also one that can actually be encountered at veterinary clinics. What is even more important is that SFTS cannot be ruled out even if tick infestation cannot be confirmed. For dogs and cats showing unexplained fever, gastrointestinal symptoms, and leukopenia/thrombocytopenia, it is necessary to include it in the differential diagnosis based on the local outbreak situation and history. Note that while favipiravir was approved in Japan in 2024 as a treatment for humans, it is important to distinguish that it has not been established as a standard treatment for dogs and cats. トップ 健康・医療 病気 Recommended for you Featured in 時事トピックス 5 articles

analysis.brief_en: The news report highlights a record high in SFTS cases in Japan, with 191 patients reported in 2025. SFTS, caused by the tick, is primarily transmitted through bites but can also be spread from infected dogs and cats to humans. The disease has been increasingly reported in both western and eastern Japan, raising concerns about its spread. SFTS can be fatal, with a case fatality rate of approximately 10–30% in Japan. In 2024, 194 cats and 12 dogs were reported to have developed the disease. Veterinary professionals are advised to implement strict infection control measures, including the use of protective gear and avoiding direct contact with infected animals. While favipiravir is approved for human treatment, it is not yet established as a standard treatment for dogs and cats. The report emphasizes the importance of vigilance and proper handling of suspected cases to prevent transmission.

elements_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: Infection control measures are extremely important when examining animals suspected of having SFTS. Veterinary professionals should use gloves, masks, gowns, eye protection, avoid direct contact with blood, saliva, excrement, be careful of bites and scratches, properly clean and disinfect instruments, and implement isolation and traffic line management for suspected cases. Favipiravir was approved in Japan in 2024 as a treatment for humans, but it has not been established as a standard treatment for dogs and cats.

supplementary_news.title: Review Links SFTS Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical Treatment Hurdles
supplementary_news.excerpt: A comprehensive review details how the tick-borne Dabie bandavirus paralyzes host immune pathways, creating severe clinical roadblocks for current antiviral therapies and vaccine development.

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Review Links SFTS Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical Treatment Hurdles by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Review Links SFTS Virus Immune Evasion to Clinical Treatment Hurdles Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive scientific review published in Frontiers in Cellular and Infection Microbiology synthesizes the growing clinical, mechanistic, and translational findings on severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus, officially classified as Dabie bandavirus. First isolated in Henan Province in 2009, this tick-borne pathogen in the genus Bandavirus, family Phenuiviridae, represents an emerging public health threat across East and Southeast Asia. National epidemiological surveillance in China from 2010 to 2023, encompassing 27,447 confirmed cases, documented an overall case fatality rate of 4.83 percent, which decreased from 12.68 percent in 2010 to 3.77 percent in 2023. However, hospital cohorts enrolling severely ill patients report substantially higher case fatality rates ranging between 12 percent and 30 percent, with intensive care mortality reaching 50 percent. Designated a priority pathogen by the World Health Organization since 2017, the virus presents a widening gap between mechanistic understanding and clinical translation, driven by its systematic dismantling of host antiviral immune pathways. The transmission ecology and geographic distribution of the virus emphasize its capacity for broader international expansion beyond recognized endemic zones. The Asian longhorned tick, Haemaphysalis longicornis, serves as the primary vector and reservoir host, demonstrating viral persistence across larvae, nymphs, and adult stages. Surveillance across central and eastern China has revealed minimum tick infection rates of 0.17 percent and pool-positive rates reaching 20.0 percent, supported by transstadial and transovarial transmission. Other tick species, including Rhipicephalus microplus, Ixodes nipponensis, and Amblyomma testudinarium, also transmit the pathogen. The detection of Haemaphysalis longicornis in the United States highlights risks of international spread. Human cases occur across China, Japan, and South Korea, with serological or animal evidence identified in Vietnam, Pakistan, Thailand, and Myanmar. Beyond tick bites, human-to-human transmission occurs through direct blood or fluid contact. A 2023 outbreak investigation in Zhejiang Province confirmed that seven of twelve cases contracted infection through direct blood exposure to a severely ill patient. The virion is an enveloped sphere measuring 80 to 120 nanometers containing three negative-sense or ambisense single-stranded RNA segments. The large segment of roughly 6,368 base pairs encodes the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase necessary for viral transcription and replication. The medium segment spans 3,378 base pairs encoding glycoprotein precursors cleaved into Gn and Gc, which mediate cellular attachment and membrane fusion. The ambisense small segment contains 1,746 base pairs, encoding nucleoprotein NP from antisense RNA and non-structural protein NSs from sense RNA. Cellular entry proceeds through clathrin-dependent endocytosis requiring an acidic endosomal environment and host cellular serine proteases. Multiple host receptors dictate cellular entry. DC-SIGN serves as a primary receptor on dendritic cells and macrophages, influencing the infection of plasmablasts. CRISPR-Cas9 screening identified chemokine receptor CCR2 as a key entry receptor binding Gn, with primary monocytes from elderly or diabetic patients showing elevated surface expression. Furthermore, knockout screening identified lipoprotein receptor-related protein 1, LRP1, as another conserved entry receptor mediating infection. The severity of infection reflects a sophisticated molecular strategy designed to paralyze host innate immune defenses. Non-structural protein NSs plays a central role by assembling viroplasm-like structures that sequester key signaling components of the type I interferon pathway, including RIG-I, TRIM25, TBK1, IKK-epsilon, and IRF3. Direct binding and sequestration of TRIM25 and TBK1 by NSs prevent IRF3 phosphorylation and nuclear translocation, thereby blocking interferon-beta transcription. Concurrently, NSs sequesters STAT2 and STAT1 into inclusion bodies, inhibiting downstream JAK-STAT signaling induced by interferons. The viral nucleoprotein NP reinforces this innate suppression through complementary mechanisms. NP promotes the autophagic degradation of cyclic GMP-AMP synthase by linking cGAS to autophagosome protein LC3. Additionally, NP triggers TUFM-dependent mitophagy to degrade mitochondrial antiviral signaling protein MAVS. By disrupting both cytosolic DNA sensing through cGAS degradation and RNA sensing through MAVS clearance, the virus disables early intracellular defenses, facilitating unchecked viral replication throughout host tissues. Alongside innate suppression, the virus severely disrupts humoral and cellular adaptive immunity. The pathogen displays a pronounced tropism for monocytes and B cells, with differentiated plasma cells acting as primary viral reservoirs exhibiting marked downregulation of the interferon pathway. Fatal infections are characterized by a failure to produce neutralizing antibodies against glycoproteins Gn and NP, indicating extensive B-cell impairment. Early monocyte apoptosis diminishes antigen presentation by dendritic cells, hindering the activation of T follicular helper cells and undermining humoral responses. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses demonstrate that circulating T lymphocytes undergo quantitative depletion and functional exhaustion, with diminished cytotoxicity correlating strongly with patient mortality. Furthermore, alterations in natural killer cell activation and macrophage polarization impair coordinated host defense. This multifaceted disruption creates a paradoxical immunological state of profound immunosuppression coupled with persistent inflammation, rendering patients incapable of mounting protective antibody responses or clearing systemic viral loads. Simultaneously, severe infection triggers a dysregulated systemic cytokine storm characterized by elevated pro-inflammatory and anti-inflammatory mediators. Hospitalized patients display markedly increased circulating levels of interleukin-1 beta, interleukin-6, interleukin-8, tumor necrosis factor alpha, interferon gamma, IP-10, MIP-1 alpha, and MCP-1. Disease severity correlates positively with concentrations of interleukin-6, IP-10, and MCP-1, while both interleukin-6 and immunosuppressive interleukin-10 remain elevated until death in fatal cases. A critical driver of this hyperinflammation is the activation of the NLRP3 inflammasome. Infection induces overexpression of Bak and activates Bax, precipitating mitochondrial DNA oxidation and subsequent cytosolic release. Cytosolic oxidized mitochondrial DNA binds to and activates the NLRP3 inflammasome, which triggers Caspase-1 activation. Catalytically active Caspase-1 cleaves pro-interleukin-1 beta and pro-interleukin-18 into mature pro-inflammatory cytokines. Monocytes and macrophages serve as primary sources of these inflammatory mediators, driving widespread vascular leakage, high fever, and tissue pathology throughout disease progression. The progression to multiorgan failure represents a complex convergence of direct viral cytopathy and immune-mediated tissue damage. Pathological examinations in fatal cases demonstrate extensive cellular destruction across vital organs. Liver tissue exhibits hepatocyte necrosis and macrophage infiltration, kidney tissue reveals mononuclear infiltration around glomeruli, and lung tissue shows alveolar rupture with inflammatory invasion. Bone marrow evaluations reveal hemophagocytosis and histiocytic hyperplasia, with severe cases progressing to hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. Central nervous system involvement occurs with viral RNA and live virus detected in cerebrospinal fluid. Pancreatic damage occurs in 17.6 percent of patients fulfilling acute pancreatitis criteria, driven by direct acinar infection via CCR2 and LRP1 alongside complement C3 hyperactivation. Additionally, the virus infects testicular Leydig cells and macrophages, inducing apoptosis and pyroptosis that decrease testosterone production. Endothelial damage is another major pathological factor; in vitro assays verify that viral infection directly causes endothelial hyperpermeability by reorganizing cytoskeletal junctions, while upregulation of soluble vascular endothelial growth factor receptor 1 inhibits angiogenesis and aggravates hemorrhage. Antiviral therapeutic options remain exceedingly limited, with significant hurdles restricting clinical efficacy. The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase inhibitor favipiravir was approved in Japan in June 2024 as the sole authorized antiviral for the disease. However, approval was granted based on a single-arm trial comparing results with historical controls rather than a randomized study. A randomized controlled trial by Li and colleagues reported overall mortality of 9.5 percent in favipiravir recipients compared to 18.3 percent in controls. Crucially, subgroup analyses demonstrated that therapeutic benefit was confined entirely to patients with low baseline viral loads exhibiting cycle threshold values of 26 or greater, where mortality fell from 11.5 percent to 1.6 percent. Favipiravir showed no significant benefit in patients with high viral loads or delayed therapy initiation. Other agents have yielded poor clinical translation; ribavirin demonstrated in vitro inhibition but failed to reduce mortality in a clinical study of 311 patients. Preclinical candidates such as VV251, an oral prodrug of 4′-fluorouridine, showed complete protection in lethal rodent models with substantially greater potency than favipiravir. Supportive clinical management remains the cornerstone of patient care, primarily involving fluid and electrolyte homeostasis, organ monitoring, and multiorgan support including mechanical ventilation and renal replacement therapy. Platelet and blood transfusions are frequently necessary to manage severe thrombocytopenia and acute hemorrhage. Controlling secondary coinfections is paramount; a multicenter study of 1,675 patients revealed that concurrent bacterial or fungal infections increased mortality from 6.7 percent to 24.3 percent. Corticosteroid use remains intensely debated, as immunosuppression can impede viral clearance and increase secondary infection risks, although co-administration with human albumin significantly lowered coinfection risks and improved clinical outcomes. Novel immunomodulatory options, including Janus kinase inhibitors like tofacitinib to dampen cytokine release and neutralizing monoclonal antibodies, are actively under evaluation. To guide timely interventions, machine-learning dynamic nomograms incorporating age, consciousness, aspartate aminotransferase, and lactate dehydrogenase have demonstrated high predictive accuracy for identifying high-risk patients needing intensive supportive therapy. Vaccine development represents the foremost preventive priority, yet formidable scientific and logistical challenges continue to impede clinical translation. Multiple preclinical platforms have demonstrated immunogenicity, including mRNA, viral vectors, protein subunits, DNA plasmids, and inactivated whole-virion vaccines. In animal models, an mRNA construct encoding glycoprotein Gc conferred 100 percent survival with immunity lasting at least six months, while a protein subunit combining Gc and nucleoprotein provided 85.7 percent protection in challenge studies. In late 2025, an international consortium initiated a first-in-human Phase I/II trial of an mRNA candidate. Nevertheless, major translation gaps persist. Most preclinical efficacy data have been derived from immunocompromised IFNAR-knockout or STAT2-knockout mouse models, which fail to reflect human immunity, particularly among older adults who face the highest risk of mortality. Furthermore, extensive viral reassortment across nine phylogenetic lineages generates genetic diversity that threatens long-term vaccine efficacy, while the low and geographically dispersed incidence of infections makes conventional Phase III efficacy trials practically infeasible. Overcoming these barriers will necessitate validated immunocompetent animal models, AI-assisted computational antigen design, and a One Health framework incorporating vector control via diatomaceous earth, natural essential oils, and anti-tick vaccines targeting antigens such as enolase. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Thursday, November 19, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Dabie Bandavirus Fatality Linked to Genotype B in Coastal East Asia by November 18, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Dabie Bandavirus Fatality Linked to Genotype B in Coastal East Asia Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome, an emerging tick-borne zoonosis caused by Dabie bandavirus, exhibits a pronounced epidemiological decoupling between infection frequency and clinical severity across mainland China. A comprehensive investigation integrating nationwide epidemiological surveillance, multi-center hospital cohorts, and large-scale viral genomics has identified an unexpected geographic divergence characterized as an inland-high-incidence versus coastal-high-fatality paradox. Between 2010 and 2023, Chinese national public health surveillance recorded 27,457 cases of the disease and 1,326 related deaths across 27 provinces and municipalities. Strikingly, spatial analysis demonstrated that transmission was overwhelmingly concentrated within seven core provinces, accounting for 99.05 percent of all reported incident infections and 99.62 percent of total recorded fatalities. Rather than displaying uniform clinical outcomes across this endemic belt, the disease presented two fundamentally distinct operational profiles. Inland provinces recorded high case volumes with comparatively low mortality, whereas maritime coastal jurisdictions experienced significantly fewer infections but suffered disproportionately severe clinical outcomes. This observed geographic divergence challenges traditional uniform surveillance models and underscores the complex interplay among viral genetics, local ecology, and regional transmission dynamics. Rigorous statistical comparison between inland provinces, comprising Henan, Hubei, and Anhui, and coastal provinces, including Zhejiang, Jiangsu, Shandong, and Liaoning, confirmed this stark epidemiological decoupling. Inland jurisdictions exhibited a combined cumulative incidence rate of 7.31 cases per 100,000 population, whereas coastal provinces recorded a substantially lower cumulative incidence rate of 3.84 cases per 100,000 population. When using the inland zone as the baseline epidemiological reference, the relative risk of acquiring an infection in coastal regions was calculated at 0.52. Conversely, case fatality rates exhibited the exact inverse trajectory between these geographic zones. The recorded case fatality rate across inland provinces was 2.61 percent, compared to 8.04 percent in coastal regions, representing a 3.08-fold elevated risk of fatal outcome for coastal patients. At the individual provincial level, this contrast was exemplified by comparing Henan and Zhejiang. To uncover the ecological drivers shaping regional transmission patterns, researchers evaluated environmental datasets spanning 2012 through 2018 using generalized additive models with an incorporated one-month time lag. Analyses focused on Xinyang in inland Henan and Zhoushan in coastal Zhejiang to quantify how ambient temperature, precipitation, and sunshine duration modulate human infection risk. The empirical modeling demonstrated that viral transmission consistently lagged ambient temperature increases by one month, corresponding to the biological interval necessary for tick vector activation and viral propagation. In inland Xinyang, transmission dynamics showed extreme climatic vulnerability, with relative risk escalating sharply once ambient temperatures crossed a 10-degree Celsius threshold, reaching peak sensitivity at 20.6 degrees Celsius with a relative risk of 4.85. Coastal Zhoushan exhibited a moderated temperature response, peaking at 22.6 degrees Celsius with a relative risk of 3.07. Crucially, coastal environments revealed a distinct meteorological threshold effect where monthly sunshine duration exceeding 200 hours triggered precipitous increases in relative risk. Overall, meteorological variables explained 82.1 percent of incidence variance in Xinyang compared to only 48.7 percent in Zhoushan, confirming climate-buffered coastal transmission. Genomic characterization of 1,820 curated viral genomes from China, Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Thailand revealed that regional clinical disparities closely align with geographic viral lineage structures. Dabie bandavirus possesses a tripartite negative-sense RNA genome consisting of Large, Medium, and Small segments that encode essential replication enzymes, envelope glycoproteins, and structural proteins. Phylogenetic reconstruction and multidimensional scaling across all three genomic segments consistently resolved five major clades, officially designated as genotypes A through E. Hierarchical clustering based on regional genotypic compositions separated the sampled geographic areas into two distinct major clades. Inland Chinese provinces clustered together into a clade dominated by high frequencies of genotype C, alongside co-circulating genotypes A and D. In contrast, coastal Zhejiang clustered directly with Japan, the Republic of Korea, and Thailand into a lineage group dominated almost exclusively by genotype B. This distinct spatial segregation established that coastal populations in East Asia are exposed to an entirely different viral population structure than patients infected across inland agricultural regions. High-resolution phylogeographic mapping within the coastal and insular environments of Zhejiang province demonstrated profound evolutionary compartmentalization that defies traditional continuous diffusion models. Despite close administrative proximity, viral populations circulating in Xiangshan county and Ningbo urban center followed completely separate micro-evolutionary paths. Constrained by its peninsular geography and active deepwater port facilities, Xiangshan harbored a highly conserved, sequestered genotype B subclade, illustrating a classic peninsular evolutionary effect where marine isolation filters gene flow. Conversely, urban Ningbo maintained broader genetic diversity comprising genotypes A, B, and C with evident mainland affinities. Across the Zhoushan archipelago, Shengsi island harbored a genotype B sublineage genetically closer to Japanese isolates than to those circulating on adjacent domestic islands, while neighboring Qushan island was dominated by genotype A lineages aligned with northern Shandong strains. Isolation-by-distance regression analysis confirmed negligible spatial correlation across these island locations, proving that geographic distance fails to predict genetic divergence in fragmented marine settings where maritime transport and discontinuous physical barriers dominate over gradual terrestrial dispersal. Genomic screening across the curated isolate dataset revealed that Zhejiang functions as an active geographic crossroads for viral reassortment and genetic recombination. The overall reassortment frequency among the 1,820 analyzed strains was 4.1 percent, characterized by discordance among the genotypes assigned to the Large, Medium, and Small segments. In Zhejiang, predominant reassortant constellations included configurations B-A-B and D-C-D, whereas Henan strains predominantly displayed mixed combinations of genotypes A, C, and D. Recombination analyses across individual genomic segments detected events in 2.6 percent of Large segments, 1.8 percent of Medium segments, and 0.4 percent of Small segments. Notably, viral isolates from coastal Zhejiang exhibited a recombination frequency of 11.0 percent, which was significantly higher than the 3.5 percent observed in inland Henan and the 3.9 percent identified in the Republic of Korea. Directional parental mapping confirmed that Zhejiang recombinants derived genomic material from diverse domestic and international lineages, indicating that coastal ecological interfaces provide fertile evolutionary ground for the emergence of novel viral variants. Discrete Bayesian phylogeographic modeling of Small-segment sequences from Zhejiang, the Republic of Korea, and Japan reconstructed complex trans-oceanic dispersal pathways operating across East Asia. The molecular clock analysis yielded a mean evolutionary substitution rate of 9.37 multiplied by 10 to the negative fifth power substitutions per site per year, placing the time to the most recent common ancestor around the year 1697. Ancestral state reconstruction supported a polyphyletic origin, identifying Hangzhou, the Republic of Korea, and Japan as supported root locations. Spatial transition matrices identified robust cross-border transmission pathways connecting the Republic of Korea to both Japanese prefectures and coastal Zhejiang centers, accompanied by counter-directional lineage seeding from Zhejiang back to the Korean peninsula. Domestically, the model detected active viral exchanges between offshore islands and mainland cities, including dispersal routes from Daishan island into Taizhou and Huzhou. These maritime transmission corridors overlap with the East Asian-Australasian Flyway, where millions of migratory shorebirds regularly transport parasitizing Haemaphysalis longicornis ticks across open maritime straits during seasonal migration. Clinical comparisons between 805 laboratory-confirmed patients in Henan and 131 patients in Zhejiang provided direct evidence linking specific viral lineages to patient outcomes. While both cohorts shared comparable demographic age and sex distributions, patients in coastal Zhejiang experienced significantly longer intervals between initial symptom onset and hospital admission, accompanied by higher clinical mortality. In the Henan cohort, genotype D infection was associated with a case fatality rate of 26.1 percent, significantly exceeding the mortality observed for genotype A at 14.4 percent and genotype C at 15.6 percent. Molecular evolutionary analysis uncovered critical adaptive signatures and specific amino acid markers that correlate with the heightened lethality of coastal infections. Selection pressure evaluations using codon-aware alignments demonstrated elevated ratios of non-synonymous to synonymous substitutions within the non-structural proteins and glycoprotein Gn of genotype B, indicating episodic positive selection or relaxed purifying pressure during viral adaptation. Genetic association models identified the RdRp-N828S substitution, located within the viral polymerase finger subdomain, as an independent molecular predictor of fatal clinical outcome, conferring an adjusted odds ratio of 2.52. Conversely, the genotype B-specific substitution RdRp-A1433T was significantly associated with reduced mortality risk, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 0.47. In addition to these functional polymerase alterations, multiple conserved structural markers, including NP-R52, Gn-S501, Gn-S218, Gc-S449, and Gc-S100, were present in over 90 percent of genotype B isolates while appearing in fewer than 10 percent of other lineages, providing definitive diagnostic targets for high-virulence genomic screening. The authors emphasized several methodological and biological caveats regarding the interpretation of these regional findings. The associations identified between specific viral genotypes, amino acid substitutions, and clinical fatality remain observational and require definitive functional validation through reverse genetics and experimental animal challenge models. Furthermore, ecological modeling relied on macro-meteorological measurements that cannot capture localized micro-environmental variables such as tick habitat density, vegetation indices, or domestic host abundance. In addition, the proposed dissemination of viral lineages via migratory birds along maritime flyways represents an epidemiologically sound hypothesis that requires direct verification through longitudinal tick screening at avian stopover sites. Finally, the statistical power of the genotype-specific survival analyses within Zhejiang was constrained by a relatively small sequenced clinical cohort compared to Henan. Despite these limitations, the evidence demonstrates that public health frameworks must transition away from uniform national guidelines toward genotype-informed precision surveillance, implementing tailored seasonal interventions across inland regions while prioritizing persistent vector management in high-fatality coastal corridors. Researchers established that a final logistic regression model based on four biological indicators achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.841 in an internal validation cohort. The predictive framework was constructed to identify patients facing elevated mortality risks during hospitalization while maintaining individual interpretability through feature attribution methods. Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome is characterized by an excessive inflammatory response and impaired adaptive immunity, carrying a substantial risk of patient mortality. The study aimed to establish and validate a machine learning-based predictive model integrating clinical and immune-inflammatory biomarkers for in-hospital mortality in patients with severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome. The investigation evaluated clinical data from a total of 238 patients diagnosed with the syndrome, comprising 177 survivors and 61 non-survivors. To train and evaluate the predictive algorithms without information leakage, the cohort was divided through stratified random sampling at a seven-to-three ratio. This split allocated 167 patients to the primary training cohort and reserved the remaining 71 patients for an independent internal validation cohort dedicated exclusively to final model testing. Candidate predictor variables were isolated using an intersection of three distinct computational screening techniques: the Boruta algorithm, the Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, and random forest recursive feature elimination. All algorithm hyperparameters were optimized exclusively within the training cohort using repeated stratified five-fold cross-validation. To demystify the internal decision-making mechanics of the resulting models, investigators applied SHapley Additive exPlanations, providing clear interpretability for the relative contribution of each selected biological feature. The resulting logistic regression model retained four decisive predictive features: severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus RNA load, CD3+CD4+ T-cell count, interleukin-6, and procalcitonin. Evaluated on the internal validation cohort of 71 patients, the model demonstrated an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.841, with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning from 0.736 to 0.930. Using the maximum Youden index derived from the training data, researchers identified an optimal cutoff probability threshold of 0.2053. When applied to the validation cohort, this threshold yielded a sensitivity of 0.944 (95 percent confidence interval: 0.742 to 0.990) and a specificity of 0.698 (95 percent confidence interval: 0.565 to 0.805), accompanied by a Brier score of 0.139 (95 percent confidence interval: 0.094 to 0.189). Assessments using calibration plots and decision curve analysis confirmed that the model offers potential net clinical benefit for hospital decision-making. To support practical point-of-care implementation, the authors translated the logistic model into both a graphical nomogram and an interactive web-based risk calculator designed for individualized mortality estimation. However, the researchers emphasized that despite these favorable internal validation metrics, rigorous multicenter prospective evaluation remains essential before the tool can be recommended for routine clinical use.
